checks.claim: The closed-form Fourier coefficients of f reproduce the numerical FFT of the closed form to ~2e-16.

checks.claim: The sign of the kernel was checked against the thermodynamic requirement that an advanced part of the front has a lower SIF, fixing C1 = -pi and f(0) < 0.

error_location.first_wrong_step: The first-order kernel is taken to be the same for all three modes (p2 = p3 = 1) and the shear coupling is taken as a pure rotation of the local frame (b2 = b3 = 1). Both differ from the Gao-Rice weights, so the slope terms do not cancel in G and every shear and front result is off.
error_location.where: submission/method.md:15-20 and 45-51; same formulas coded in submission/solve.py:42-54
explains_groups: Part B: loading level and front amplitude

notes: Only C1, S1 and K10_scaled match the reference, because p1 = 1 and the Irwin weight m3 = 1/(1-nu) are right; s_kappa3_max also passes within tolerance. The wrong theory is exactly the usual mistake in KEY_NOTES.md section 3 (mode-1 weight on all modes, slope couplings of 1 and 1). Because b2 != m3*b3 the solver gets a nonzero SG and an antisymmetric piece of f, which is why the tables fail even where a single sample happens to land inside tolerance (f[9], kappa1[9], kappa2[10], kappa3[8]). The five claimed checks only verify internal consistency of this wrong theory; they do not compare with an independent solution. Rice 1985 is named but not derived, and no three-dimensional elasticity computation is in the folder. Large binary files under tmp/ were left out of the copy and are irrelevant.
